notes: Volume G–I of the collection: 57 pages, 39 entries (24 under G, 21 under H when the Hertzka and Hertzka & Knowles entries are counted separately, 1 under I) covering architects, builders, developers, landscape architects and firms whose names begin G, H or I, read end to end — the title page, the three letter indexes, every entry (education, firms, cultural identification, narrative and footnotes), every 'Works in San Francisco' / 'Projects in San Francisco' and 'Other notable projects' list, and every figure caption. This is the third of the eight letter-range PDFs on the collection's landing page; A–C and D–F are done. There is no inventory table and no APN anywhere in the document, so the record-parcel check resolve_eas.py's report prints has nothing to test against. The project lists are the dense seam again, and this volume shifts the mix: two-thirds of its addresses come from five builder entries (Galli, Harrington, Heilmann, the two Hinkels) rather than from architects, so the overlap with the Sunset, Oceanside, Parkside and Eureka Valley material this repo already carries is much heavier than in D–F. Six entries yielded nothing numbered: Gensler, Graves, Guzzardo and Homsey list only unnumbered civic and landscape projects, Hurd's list is a cross-reference to Masten & Hurd, and Hillmer's only San Francisco work is his own office.

coverage.note: 198 numbered-address mentions across 57 pages became 176 findings. The gap is deduplication and the unnumbered: 22 project-list lines name a tract, a corner or a block face with no street number ("23rd and Ocean Avenues", "Corner of Pine and Baker", "2800 block of Clay Street"), and the rest are addresses printed more than once — Wayne Hertzka's list and the Hertzka & Knowles firm list are nearly the same eleven buildings, each biography opens with a figure caption naming an address from its own list, and the narrative repeats what the list already gave. Each project was recorded once, credited to the firm where the volume has a firm entry, with the variant year or street type kept in extra. 145 of the 176 reached a parcel and 31 did not: 13 recorded ranges now split across separate parcels (109-125 Beaumont, 1209-1219 2nd Avenue, 123-173 7th Avenue, 4529-4551 California, 126-174 11th Avenue, 107-163 14th Avenue, 106-162 15th Avenue, 1700-1738 8th Avenue, 1558-1586 46th Avenue, 1017-1019 Green, 751-753 Cole, 209-233 Central, and 1301-1307 Lake, which is four condominium parcels), 8 numbers the city no longer has (1590 39th Avenue, 319 Grant, 1100 Mission, 1101 Tennessee, 148 Sansome, 2249 9th Avenue, 2117 Market, 1901 Van Ness), 6 condominiums, 2 ranges printed in a form with no readable pair of numbers (48-52Kearny, 555/575 Market), 1 street the address register does not hold (8 Fisherman's Wharf) and 1 — 1 Letterman Drive — whose parcel is the whole Presidio reservation. Of the 145, 115 were published onto 115 pages (63 created by this run) across 25 neighborhood directories, and 30 were declined: 27 already carried by a survey or statement that documented the building first, 2 on parcels with no 2025 secured-roll row, 1 a second street number on a page already carrying the fact.
